meanings.note: Informal greeting.
Informal farewell.
Imperatives match address: scusa / scusami (informal tu), scusi (polite lei), scusate (plural voi).

examples.trans: Excuse me, where is the exit?

meanings.note: Marks beneficiary (per i ragazzi), duration/target (quanto per Corinna?), or reason (scusa per prima).
Refers to an earlier moment (scusa per prima, 'sorry about earlier').
Standard negative particle placed immediately before the verb (plus any clitics).

sapere.gloss: to know (a fact or how to)

meanings.note: Knowing facts or answers (sa dov'è?, non lo so).
Followed directly by an infinitive (sai giocare?, 'do you know how to play?').

examples.trans: Do you know how to play foosball?

meanings.note: Interrogative or exclamative word before verbs or nouns.
Conjunction or relative pronoun linking two clauses.

examples.trans: They say that it is true.

meanings.note: Unstressed 1st-person singular direct, indirect, or reflexive pronoun (mi sento, mi piace, mi serve).
Identity, description, location, and passive/intransitive auxiliary; with ci forms c'è ('there is').
Impersonal/3rd-person verb with essere in the past (che mi è successo, 'what happened to me').

examples.text: Non so che mi è successo.
examples.trans: I do not know what came over me.

meanings.note: First-person singular subject pronoun; usually included for contrast or emphasis.
Marks possession, material, department (stagista di regia), or topic.
Links verbs like dire, chiedere, pensare to a following infinitive.
Di solito is the standard two-word phrase for 'usually'.
Indefinite article: un before most masculine nouns, uno before s + consonant/z, una (un') before feminine nouns.
Everyday word for a young woman or girlfriend.

examples.trans: She is a likeable young woman.

meanings.note: Absolute superlative (-issimo) of normale.

examples.trans: It is a completely normal day.
I am a very ordinary person.

meanings.note: Introduces a condition (se vuoi, se ti va, se no 'otherwise').

examples.text: Se ti va, prendiamo un caffè.
examples.trans: If you fancy it, let us get a coffee.

meanings.note: Expresses desire or intention; imperfect volevo softens a polite request.
Conversational bridge moving a talk forward or drawing a conclusion.
Temporal sense in narratives.
Also used idiomatically: darsi del tu (use informal 'you'), dare venti anni (guess someone's age).
Contraction of preposition di + masculine singular article il.

examples.trans: It is not from your department.

meanings.note: Familiar singular subject pronoun; darsi del tu means addressing each other informally.
Links a time clause or asks 'when?'.

examples.trans: When I get back, I will call you.

tornare.gloss: to return; to go / come back

meanings.en: to come back; to go back
meanings.note: Present tense often expresses a firm plan for tomorrow (torno domani).

examples.trans: I am coming back tomorrow morning.
When do you get back from work?

meanings.note: Contraction of preposition da + masculine singular article il.

examples.trans: I step out of the theatre.

meanings.note: Buon lavoro! wishes colleagues a good workday.

Marks constant repetition or habit.
Feminine singular definite article (la scena, la regia).
Third-person feminine singular direct object clitic (non la dico, la risolviamo).
Used with fare or farsi (farsi la doccia, 'to take a shower').
Marks accompaniment, instrument, or attitude.
Used for washing or cleaning.
Invariable colour adjective (una spugna viola, due spugne viola).
Links words or clauses; distinct from accented è, meaning is.
Invariable compound noun built from bagno (bath) + schiuma (foam).

examples.trans: I buy a scented body wash.

meanings.note: Having a pleasant fragrance.

meanings.note: Stai fermo ('stay still'), stare in porta ('play in goal').

examples.trans: I am writing a note right now.
